subject: Renewal & mid-contract uplift — multi-year option and co-term path for CatalystAI
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@catalystai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and uplift discussion for 2027

Hi Priya,

Hope you’re well — we’re starting planning for our contract renewal (Mar 2027) and have an in-year growth event: we expect usage to increase ~45% over the next 6 months because of a new generative feature rollout.

Two asks from our side:
- Do you have a clear path to accommodate a mid-contract uplift with pro-rata billing? We need predictable invoice treatment.
- We’re exploring a 3-year co-term to lock pricing, but procurement wants visibility on multi-year discounts and early-exit provisions.

Can you share options and a ballpark uplift rate or discount for a 3-year commitment vs annual renew? Also cc'ing procurement.

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Product Manager
CatalystAI
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, procurement@catalystai.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and uplift discussion for 2027

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up. High level options we typically recommend:

1) Mid-contract uplift (short-term top-up): pro-rata invoice for the remainder of the period + option to convert to committed capacity at a reduced uplift (we recommend a 15% uplift on top of current unit rates for immediate top-ups; that delta declines if you annualize the additional usage).

2) Multi-year (3-year) co-term: we can offer a blended discount ladder (3% off year 1 list on baseline commit, 6% off year 2 if you maintain or grow, 10% off year 3 on baseline + agreed uplift band). Early-exit: standard recoupment on unused committed credits for year(s) remaining; we can add a soft-exit clause tied to M&A or force majeure.

3) Hybrid: immediate top-up to cover the rollout (pro-rata months) + convert that top-up into a new committed band at renewal, with a signing credit applied now to offset the Q4 invoice.

A few clarifying Qs to size this correctly:
- Do you want the uplift to be an immediate purchase (cover next 3 months) or a committed increase that starts at your Mar renewal?
- Will you accept a stepped discount tied to maintaining >=X% of baseline usage?

I’ll draft a concrete quote showing the three options and the expected monthly invoices for each. Can we sync for 30 mins Mon/Tue next week?

Thanks — Priya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Renewal and uplift discussion for 2027 — sizing and discount math

Hi all — notes from the call and the sizing model attached (summary below).

Summary: based on projected feature rollout, estimated incremental tokens/month = 42M. Two preferred structures:

A) Fast top-up + convert: One-off pro-rata top-up for Oct–Feb at current unit rate + 12% uplift surcharge for on-demand capacity. At renewal, convert the top-up to committed capacity and apply a 5% conversion credit to the first renewal invoice.

B) Immediate committed add-on + multi-year discount: Add a committed uplift starting now for the remainder of 2026 and formalize into a 3-year co-term at renewal. Pricing we modeled: 4% blended discount for 3-year total if baseline is held, escalating to 7% if you maintain >=95% of committed utilization. We can offer a signing credit equal to 1 month of uplift consumption if you sign the 3-year by Oct 31.

Notes on split invoicing: we’ll provide separate invoice lines for baseline vs uplift; finance can map to distinct GL codes.

Attaching a worked example and a draft quote (CatalystAI_Renewal_Quote_v3.pdf) and a draft SOW. Priya will follow up with contract language for the early-exit and soft-exit clauses.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solution Strategy — Redwood Inference
